suitability.note: A generated GLB carries measured bounds and surfaces, so the single-image intake steps that recover structure from one photo are not applicable here.

definitionOfDone: Every part in the download renders from embedded data with no runtime asset fetch.
Part identity is labelled as a hypothesis until a render review confirms it.
Colour, roughness and metalness are measured from the source, not invented.
Every clip is seeked to at least 5 times and its binding delta compared against its own track values (Gate R1).
Every VFX emitter resolves to a socket measured on a bone the rig really has.
Effect and light colours are measured off the character or a stated HSL move from one.
notDone: AI-vision review against the reference (the skill's stage 4) has not run. The renders in evidence/renders are captures, not a scored comparison sheet.
Hidden sides are whatever the generator hallucinated; a single photo cannot confirm them.
No skin-integrity sweep (G10). Tearing under motion was not measured over a pose sweep; nothing in this build claims it was.
No foot-contact gate (G8). The source clips' footSlide was not measured, so 'skating' is not ruled out on any of them.
The part label "body-shell" is still a bounds hypothesis at confidence 0.20. Only the BONE names are confirmed.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: figure height 1.9 model units (source generator: Tripo auto-rig)

measuredCorrection.note: The 'front' line above says the subject faces -z. Measurement disagrees and the measurement wins: the arm span runs along Z (2.57 units against a 1.01-unit body depth), so Z is the LATERAL axis, and the dark eye cluster sits on the +X side of the Head joint, so +X is the face. The camera exported in MONSTER_CUTE_CAMERA points at the character's back.

materials.name: body shell surface

albedo.samplingNotes: per-vertex colour sampled from the source albedo texture at each vertex UV; the factor above is the multiplier, not the colour

metalness.source: median of the source metallic-roughness texture over this part

materials.normal: source had a normal map; NOT carried (vertex normals only)
materials.notes: Measured from the generated GLB, not authored. Refine by observation against the reference.
materials.emissiveDrivenAtRuntime: src/vfx drives material.emissive and emissiveIntensity for the idle aura, the charge glow and the impact flash. The base colour and the vertex colours are never touched.

buildPasses.goal: Proportions and part layout from the measured GLB bounds.
Part surfaces carried as measured geometry with locked seams.
Per-vertex albedo and per-part roughness/metalness medians from the source.
Pivots per part exist; authored motion, sockets and destruction groups are still to do.

intakeSteps: clips: preset:climb (3.50s), preset:dive (2.75s), preset:hurt (13.88s), preset:jump (2.25s), preset:shoot (9.08s)
glbBaseline.note: Surfaces are the GLB's measured triangles, quantised and embedded as code; the GLB itself is not shipped or fetched. Part names are bounds hypotheses.

animationAnchors: root group supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale and visibility
group.userData.pivots[<part-id>] is a pivot group at each part's bounds centre
group.userData.update(elapsedSeconds) drives the built-in idle motion

risks.note: Part names come from bounds bands; a boot can be called a knee pad. Confirm in the viewer before publishing.
Back and underside geometry is generated, not observed.
Colour resolution equals vertex density; decimation lowers both.
A rigged single shell has no part decomposition, so destruction anchors do not exist for this model. Nothing was invented to substitute.
hornArc, hearts, beam and impactFlash are bound by CLIP NAME. No kinematic feature separates anger from any other in-place gesture. Marked 'inferred' in the spec, in the code and in the viewer UI.

The viewer cancels the hip's planar travel by default so the figure stays framed. Locomotion clips then skate: that is what their real 1.3H-2.6H travel looks like once the world stops moving. Toggle it off to see the untouched motion.

The belly self-shadowed in stripes under animation and read as a torn mesh. Cause was the shadow map, not the skin: a wide band of that surface is near-perpendicular to the key light. Fixed with shadow.normalBias = 0.035H. Confirmed by moving the light with the pose frozen, which removed it while the geometry was untouched. Reweighting and dual quaternion skinning were both measured and both rejected — DQS made the fold metrics worse, because there was no linear-blend collapse to fix.

actionProfile.provenance: This block did NOT ship in the playground export. The socket SET below was authored; every socket POSITION was measured (tools/measure.ts) and every socket names a bone this rig really has.

vfx.provenance: img2threejs has no particle, trail or shader subsystem — the skill emits geometry, materials, a rig and clips and stops there. Everything under src/vfx/ is hand-written for this showcase in plain three.js with no added dependency, and no texture files: the round sprite is cut in a fragment shader and the heart is a THREE.Shape.
vfx.colourPolicy: Every effect colour is a measured region colour or a stated HSL move away from one. src/characterProfile.ts ACCENT. Nothing was picked by eye.

effects.basis: ambient; uses the emissive channel the spec measured as #000000, i.e. unused
measured — bound when handRange >= 0.40H or the clip classifies dash/run
measured — bound when the clip is not 'planted'; each puff is triggered by the sole socket crossing the ground band while descending
measured — bound when rise >= 0.15H; magnitude read from the hip's fall speed at contact
INFERRED — bound on clips NAMED angry/freaky/frustrated
measured on 'gesture' clips; INFERRED on the clip named shoot

effects.anchor: effect:palm.r, aimed along the measured head-local forward vector
effects.basis: INFERRED — fired on the clip named shoot, and on the manual 'blast' cue
INFERRED — bound on the clip named heart_pose
INFERRED — on the clip named hurt, and on the manual 'hurt' cue

vfx.destructionGroups: NOT AVAILABLE. The spec carries no destructionGroups and cannot: rigging merged the surface, so this model is a single skinned shell of 192,082 triangles with one part hypothesis ("body-shell", confidence 0.20). There is no part decomposition to break apart, and no destruction anchor was invented to stand in for one.

rig.source: src/rigData.ts, embedded by the playground export
rig.boneNameNote: These are the rig's own joint names, not the bounds-derived part hypotheses that carry the 0.20 confidence elsewhere in this spec. The hypothesis warning applies to the PART label "body-shell"; it does not apply to Root/Hip/Pelvis/Head/L_Hand/R_ToeBase and the rest.
rig.decimation: REFUSED. The rigged model is one skinned shell at a single level of detail. A decimate pass rewrites the vertex set, so skinIndex/skinWeight would point at vertices that no longer exist and the figure would tear the moment a clip ran. geometryDescriptor.decimate is absent from this spec and must stay absent while the rig is bound.

gateR1.criterion: maxSampledBindingDelta <= 2^-23 over >= 5 sampled times x every clip

scaleDeltaTripwire.note: no clip moves a joint's scale away from its rest value (max 6.00e-7, limit 1e-6). Every one of the 1,353 tracks does carry a scale channel, but each holds the rest value; the rest pose itself is 1 +/- 1.07e-5, which is exporter quantisation, not animation.

animation.loopRule: poseReturn <= 0.5 deg per rotation joint AND hipReturn <= 0.01H, measured per clip

runtime.mixer: THREE.AnimationMixer, advanced with the frame DELTA (never elapsed time)
runtime.crossFade: 0.28 s by default on every clip change; a hard cut pops on the first frame
runtime.api: createAnimator(rigged) -> play(name|index, fade), seek(name, t), stop(), update(dt)
runtime.autoRepeat: 29 of 33 clips do not return to their first pose, so by the measured loop rule they are one-shots. The viewer restarts them by cross-fading the clip into a clone of itself. This hides a discontinuity that is really there; it does not make the clip loop, and loops() keeps reporting the measurement.

lighting.policy: every light takes its colour from a measured region of the character

lights.why: the only slightly warm colour on the figure

lighting.note: createMonsterCuteLookDevLights() (neutral white) is still exported and is the right rig for judging surface colour.

shadow.why: normalBias rather than depth bias: the belly is a large gently curved surface whose normal runs nearly perpendicular to the key across a wide band, which is the worst case for a shadow map. A depth bias large enough to clear it detaches the contact shadow under the feet.
